summary: Phase 2 (Live Dashboard, Online Classes CRUD, Filtered Exports) + Phase 1 regression validated. 61/62 pytest cases pass (Phase 2 suite 28/29 + Phase 1 suite 33/33). One real backend bug: slug mass-assignment on POST /api/online-classes. Admin UI end-to-end verified: login works, Live Dashboard renders real KPIs + snapshot timestamp refreshes, Online Classes page creates/lists/edits/deletes classes, Enquiries/Students/Batches ExportButton triggers actual browser downloads for CSV/XLSX/PDF.

critical.issue: Slug mass-assignment protection broken. onlineClasses.js L78 does `slugify(req.body.slug || payload.title)` reading req.body.slug BEFORE the ALLOWED_FIELDS whitelist. A client supplying `{title:'X',slug:'garbage-slug'}` has the attacker-controlled slug persisted (slugified) instead of deriving it from title. Spec explicitly states slug must be derived server-side from title. Fix: use `slugify(payload.title)` only (ignore req.body.slug), or remove 'slug' acceptance entirely.

minor.issue: Content-Disposition filename is `ssci-enquiries-&-leads-{ts}.csv` because dataset label 'Enquiries & Leads' is lowercased/space-joined but '&' is preserved. Spec called for `ssci-enquiries-{ts}.csv`. Consider stripping non-alphanumerics in safeFilename slug (same for 'ssci-students-roster-...', 'ssci-batches-schedule-...').

status field is in ALLOWED_FIELDS, so clients can create a class directly in 'Active' status, bypassing a Draft→Active workflow. Review spec says 'default status Draft' - OK as default - but consider server-forcing status='Draft' on create and only allowing transition via PUT.
followUpDate is stored as string on Lead model; defensive parsing with new Date() is lenient (accepts e.g. '2026/13/40'). Low-impact but a strict ISO regex guard would be safer.

issues: course select uses native HTML <select> (observed tagName=SELECT) instead of a shadcn/Radix Select; inconsistent with rest of admin UI styling. Not blocking.

action_items: FIX: In /app/backend/server/routes/onlineClasses.js, replace `slugify(req.body.slug || payload.title)` with `slugify(payload.title)` so the slug is always derived from the server-trusted title (mass-assignment protection).
Clean up export filenames: strip '&' and ambiguous chars from the dataset-label slug used in Content-Disposition (expected `ssci-enquiries-{ts}.csv`, actual `ssci-enquiries-&-leads-{ts}.csv`).
Consider forcing status='Draft' on POST /api/online-classes and only allowing status transitions through PUT.
(Carried over from iter_2) Confirm NODE_ENV=production on prod deploy so CORS allowlist is enforced.
critical_code_review_comments: onlineClasses.js reads unvetted req.body.slug before whitelisting - classic mass-assignment smell. The ALLOWED_FIELDS pattern is applied to payload but then bypassed for slug derivation. All derived identifiers (id, slug) must come exclusively from whitelisted or server-generated values.

exports.js is 390+ lines combining filter builders, dataset config, CSV/XLSX/PDF writers, and route wiring - fine for Phase 2 but on the edge of maintainability. If PDF styling evolves, split writers into /routes/exports/{csv,xlsx,pdf}.js.

Dashboard analytics performs Lead.find({}).lean() to compute follow-up buckets in Node. For large lead sets this is O(n) over the wire; a Mongo aggregation using $facet / $cond on parsed dates would scale better once leads > 10k.
Dashboard payload leaks nothing sensitive but conversionRate is rounded in server (good); confirm the UI handles conversionRate=0 when totalLeads=0 (verified visually - shows '0%' correctly).

rca of the issue: Mass-assignment slug bug RCA: In /app/backend/server/routes/onlineClasses.js the create handler calls `pickAllowed(req.body)` which correctly filters payload to the ALLOWED_FIELDS whitelist (which does NOT include 'slug'). Immediately after however, line 78 computes `const baseSlug = slugify(req.body.slug || payload.title);` - reading `req.body.slug` directly from the raw request, defeating the whitelist. Reproduction: `POST /api/online-classes {title:'QA Online Python Masters', slug:'garbage-slug'}` returns `onlineClass.slug === 'garbage-slug'` instead of `'qa-online-python-masters'`. Mitigation: change line 78 to `const baseSlug = slugify(payload.title);` (or `slugify(payload.title) || slugify(req.body.slug)` is still wrong - must be title-derived only per spec).
